prompt:
You are controlling a network client (Redis). Your instruction: Send PING, then GET mykey, then stop sending commands.

Already done at the start of this session, and not to be sent again: execute_redis_command {"command":"PING"}; execute_redis_command {"command":"GET mykey"}. Answer the latest message with what your instruction calls for next; if nothing is left to do, answer with no actions.

# Response Format
Return ONE JSON object {"actions": [ ... ]} holding every action to perform now, in order. Return {"actions": []} to do nothing now (or `wait_for_more` when a reply is incomplete and more is coming). JSON only — no prose, no code fences; an optional <reasoning>…</reasoning> block may precede it.
`set_memory` / `append_memory` keep notes that are shown to you as "Memory:" on every later call; what happened earlier in this session is shown above the event when the client keeps history.

# Available actions
redis_subscribe

Subscribe to channels (SUBSCRIBE), glob patterns (PSUBSCRIBE) or shard channels (SSUBSCRIBE). Each confirmation arrives as redis_subscription_changed and each message as redis_message_received. Not available in cluster mode.

Parameters:
- channels: array (optional) - Channel names to subscribe to
- patterns: array (optional) - Glob patterns to subscribe to, e.g. news.*
- shard_channels: array (optional) - Shard channel names to subscribe to

Example:
```json
{
  "type": "redis_subscribe",
  "channels": [
    "news"
  ],
  "patterns": [
    "alerts.*"
  ]
}
```

redis_unsubscribe

Unsubscribe. Name channels, patterns or shard_channels to drop those; an empty list drops every subscription of that kind; no field at all drops everything this connection holds.

Parameters:
- channels: array (optional) - Channels to unsubscribe from ([] for all)
- patterns: array (optional) - Patterns to unsubscribe from ([] for all)
- shard_channels: array (optional) - Shard channels to unsubscribe from ([] for all)

Example:
```json
{
  "type": "redis_unsubscribe",
  "channels": [
    "news"
  ]
}
```

redis_publish

Publish a message to a channel (PUBLISH, or SPUBLISH with shard). While this connection is subscribed on RESP2 it cannot publish itself, so the client publishes over a short second connection to the same server.

Parameters:
- channel: string (required) - The channel to publish on
- message: string (required) - The message text
- shard: boolean (optional) - true to publish on a shard channel (SPUBLISH)

Example:
```json
{
  "type": "redis_publish",
  "channel": "news",
  "message": "hello"
}
```

execute_redis_command

Execute a Redis command

Parameters:
- command: string (required) - Redis command as typed at redis-cli (e.g. GET key, SET greeting "hello world"). Quote an argument that contains spaces with double or single quotes.

Example:
```json
{
  "type": "execute_redis_command",
  "command": "GET mykey"
}
```

disconnect

Disconnect from the Redis server

Example:
```json
{
  "type": "disconnect"
}
```

wait_for_more

Take no action and wait for more data from the server. Use when the reply so far is incomplete.

Example:
```json
{
  "type": "wait_for_more"
}
```

set_memory

Replace this server's (or client's) memory with new content; the old memory is discarded. Memory is shown to the model with every event, is shared by all of the instance's connections and outlives each one, unlike the history of a single connection, which ends with it. Keep here anything needed later by every connection: data you stored, counters, settings.

Parameters:
- value: string (required) - New memory value as a string. Replaces all existing memory.

Example:
```json
{
  "type": "set_memory",
  "value": "users_created: alice,bob\nnext_order_id: 1043"
}
```

append_memory

Add lines to this server's (or client's) memory; existing memory is kept. A line written `key: value` replaces an earlier line with the same key instead of adding a second one. Memory is shown to the model with every event, is shared by all of the instance's connections and outlives each one.

Parameters:
- value: string (required) - Text to append as a string, one fact per line. A `key: value` line replaces the earlier line with that key; any other line is added after the existing memory.

Example:
```json
{
  "type": "append_memory",
  "value": "connection_count: 5\nfiles_uploaded: 3"
}
```

notify_operator

Show a note to the person operating NetGet, on their own screen. It is NOT sent over the network: the peer, client or server on the other end never sees it. To say anything to them, use this protocol's own send or response action.

Parameters:
- message: string (required) - The note for the operator (never transmitted)

Example:
```json
{
  "type": "notify_operator",
  "message": "Server #1 is listening on port 8080"
}
```
